lines.text: as also on what it has denied us and that in which we our-
selves have been found wanting. No doubt the result will be
different in each individual case if we weigh things up and
see whether the profit or loss has been the greater; very
different the measure of joy or sorrow, of thankfulness or
bitterness in our hearts. But there can be no doubt of this,
namely, that each one of us should be thankful. Even he to
whom the term has brought distress and disappointment,
and who is haunted by the tormenting sense of the un-
attained, of having trodden devious paths. He too who would
like to echo the words of the poet:
"How precious is the coming day, O my judge! How one
dreams of wandering in the mountains and of great things!
But the day that has just died is terrible; unwillingly,
regretfully we look back on it, as on a rubbish heap."
Should not even such a one feel obliged to be thankful?
For if he honestly faces the bitterness of his inner self-
judgment, must he not confess that in consequence he should
be purer and more experienced? But may he affirm this to
himself? Now, it is exactly to such a man that the word
applies: "My peace I give you. Not as the world gives, give
I to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be
afraid!" For has he not been pursuing a false peace? A
peace such as the world gives and which he sought to attain
himself and by his own resources? The peace of God can
only be given him; and it will be given when such a person
turns his attention away from time and from thoughts of
self, and is ready for the peace of eternity: "My peace I leave
with you. My peace I give to you!"
But this word of Scripture applies no less to those who are
looking back on the term with glad and thankful hearts: on
its tasks which inspired increasing ability, on their progress
in knowledge and understanding, and on the enrichment of
their lives through social intercourse and fellowship with
others. They too must take to heart this word of Scripture:
"My peace I give you; not as the world gives, give I to you"
lest from grateful joy they should fall into complacency and
self-satisfaction.
